text:
A finite lifetime produces a natural energy uncertainty (linewidth) of order

\[
\Delta E \sim \frac{\hbar}{\tau}.
\]

Thus,

\[
\Delta E_1\sim \frac{6.58\times10^{-16}\,\text{eV·s}}{10^{-9}\,\text{s}}
=6.58\times10^{-7}\,\text{eV},
\]

\[
\Delta E_2\sim \frac{6.58\times10^{-16}\,\text{eV·s}}{10^{-8}\,\text{s}}
=6.58\times10^{-8}\,\text{eV}.
\]

To resolve the two levels clearly, their separation must be larger than their combined broadening,

\[
\Delta E_1+\Delta E_2\approx 7.2\times10^{-7}\,\text{eV}.
\]

Using \(\hbar/(2\tau)\) instead changes this only by a factor of two. Among the choices, only \(10^{-4}\,\text{eV}\) is comfortably larger than the level widths.

Answer: B
